question.problem:
Negate the following statement: 

$\,$ Some rational numbers are not proper fractions.
question.worked_solution:
The given statement can be re-phrased as follows:

$\,$ There exists $x\in Q$ such that $x$ is not a proper fraction.

Introducing the existential quantifier, we get the following:

$\,$ $∃x\in Q,\,x\text{ is not a proper fraction}.$

Negating this, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(∃x\in Q,\,x\text{ is not a proper fraction}) & ≡∀x\in Q,\,¬(x\text{ is not a proper fraction}) \\  & ≡∀x\in Q,\,x\text{ is a proper fraction}\end{aligned}
$$

which reads 

$\,$ For all $x\in Q,$ $x\text{ is a proper fraction}.$

or simply

$\,$ All rational numbers are proper fractions.
